title: Most of an organism's structure is due to inheritance, not current use

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Most of an organism's structure is due to inheritance, not current use

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The chief part of each organism's structure is simply inherited, so that many structures, such as the shared bones of monkey arm, horse leg, bat wing and seal flipper, have no direct relation to the species' present habits of life.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: by far the most important consideration is that the chief part of the organisation of every being is simply due to inheritance; and consequently, though each being assuredly is well fitted for its place in nature, many structures now have no direct relation to the habits of life of each species.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Organs of small importance.”. Scope: all organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phylogenetic comparative data can quantify inheritance for selected traits and clades. The organism-wide universal and the amount meant by 'chief part' prevent complete resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Partition morphological variation into phylogenetic inheritance and association with current ecology using comparative models across clades. Strong phylogenetic signal after controlling for present habits supports the claim; predominantly ecology-specific structure would oppose it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Chief part' lacks a natural unit of measurement.

Inheritance and adaptation are not mutually exclusive explanations.

operationalizability: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: For the limb example and for bird and mammal ecology, open trees and trait tables support a standard comparative partition, and that analysis is weeks of work for a restricted scope. The claim is about most of the organization of every organism, which existing matrices do not cover. A correlation with current habits also would not prove that a trait arose for those habits, so the test is informative only for the mismatch Darwin named.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Partition skeletal characters among mammals or birds into phylogenetic signal versus diet, habitat, and locomotion from trait databases. The claim is supported if most characters, including the shared limb skeleton, track clade membership rather than present habits; it is refuted if current ecology explains the chief part of structure.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Trait databases cover a small slice of 'the chief part of organisation', mostly vertebrates.

Phylogenetic signal can reflect constraint or low power rather than inheritance of unused structure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.68
data existence: 0.72
